description: Real runs of coach.py with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1: one question with retrieval, the same question without retrieval, and a question with no matching knowledge.
notes: Each case was one separate command. Its report was written with --output to a temporary file and is copied here unchanged.
The citation check only checks source IDs, not whether each sentence of an answer is true.
These are three smoke runs, not an evaluation. They do not show whether retrieval makes answers better or worse.

cases.name: rag
cases.command: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python coach.py --question 'Must the inspector require Vector to guess the exact midpoint?'
cases.question: Must the inspector require Vector to guess the exact midpoint?
cases.answer:
The inspector does not require Vector to guess the exact midpoint; instead, they check that Vector's guesses lie within the range that is still possible at that moment. [reliability-midpoint-not-required]  

This strategy stays inside the range and passes the inspector regardless of whether the guess is the exact midpoint or not. [reliability-inspector-checks]  

Yes, the inspector checks Vector's guesses to ensure they are within the range, not necessarily requiring them to be the exact midpoint. [reliability-inspector-checks]

sources.title: Exact middle not required
sources.text:
The inspector checks that each of Vector's guesses lies inside the range
that is still possible at that moment. It does not require the guess to be
exactly the middle of that range. Another strategy that stays inside the
range would also pass the inspector.

sources.title: What the inspector checks
sources.text:
The inspector checks that the duel was still running and had rounds left,
that the settings and both secret numbers did not change, that exactly one
round was added and earlier rounds stayed the same, that both guesses are
whole numbers inside the range, that both hints match the secret numbers,
that Vector's range matches its whole history, and that the status
(playing, win or draw) is correct.

sources.title: Guessing Vector's number yourself
sources.text:
The fastest safe way to find Vector's number is the same method: guess the
middle of the numbers that are still possible and use each hint to cut the
range in half. With this method you also need at most 5 guesses on Easy,
7 on Normal and 6 on Hard. On Easy and Normal Vector always finds your
number within the limit, so to win you must guess its number in an
earlier round than it guesses yours. Guessing in the same round gives a
draw.
